data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Jariya means 'she who carries.' In the Islamic context, this name is derived from the Quranic verse, 'And indeed, We have given you, [O Muhammad], a clear victory. So put your trust in Allah and rely upon Him. And enough is your Lord as a Guardian. The name Jariya carries the meaning “Carrier of good news, glad tidings” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Parents who choose Jariya usually hope their child will grow to embody carrier of good news, glad tidings and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Jariya bint Abi Bakr was a famous female Sufi scholar and poetess of the Abbasid period. She was known for her spiritual insights and poetic compositions, and is considered a significant figure in the development of Sufi thought and literature.
historical_references.context: The Abbasid Caliphate was the dominant Islamic political power during this period, and Sufism, a mystical form of Islam that emphasized personal devotion and inner spiritual experience, was beginning to emerge as a distinct spiritual tradition.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Jariya was a 13th century Andalusian scholar and historian who wrote extensively about Islamic history and culture. His most famous work, the 'Al-Tarikh al-Kabir' or 'The Great History', is a comprehensive history of the Islamic world from the earliest times to the 13th century.
historical_references.context: Islam had spread to Spain and other parts of Europe during this period, and the Andalusian scholars played a significant role in preserving and transmitting Islamic knowledge to the wider world. Ibn Jariya's work was an important contribution to this intellectual tradition.
